title.es: Proyecto de escritura: edición de precisión

es: Editar un borrador con precisión: corregir tiempos, registro, cohesión, conectores y concisión eligiendo el cambio mínimo.

vocabulary.es: releer para detectar erratas y deslices

teaching.en: We edit in layers: meaning first, then cohesion, then wording, and a final proofread for the slips that survive every earlier pass.
teaching.es: Editamos por capas: primero el significado, después la cohesión, luego la redacción y, al final, una relectura para detectar los deslices que sobreviven a todas las pasadas anteriores.
teaching.explanationEs: Revisar todo a la vez hace perder errores; cada capa tiene su propia pregunta.
segments: We edit in layers: meaning first, then cohesion, then wording, and
a final proofread for the slips that survive every earlier pass.
teaching.audioText: We edit in layers: meaning first, then cohesion, then wording, and a final proofread for the slips that survive every earlier pass.

teaching.en: A connector must mirror the real logic of the ideas: in We cut the price; as a result, sales rose, it signals consequence, whereas however would suggest an unexpected contrast.
teaching.es: Un conector debe reflejar la lógica real de las ideas: en Bajamos el precio; como resultado, las ventas subieron, señala consecuencia, mientras que however sugeriría un contraste inesperado.
teaching.explanationEs: Suma (moreover), contrasta (however) o da resultado (as a result): elige según la relación real.
segments: A connector must mirror the real logic of the ideas: in We cut the price;
as a result, sales rose, it signals consequence, whereas however would suggest an unexpected contrast.
teaching.audioText: A connector must mirror the real logic of the ideas: in We cut the price; as a result, sales rose, it signals consequence, whereas however would suggest an unexpected contrast.

teaching.en: A wordy sentence buries its point, so tighten up the draft: In order to finish, we need time becomes To finish, we need time, and the meaning is untouched.
teaching.es: Una frase prolija entierra su idea, así que ajusta el borrador: In order to finish, we need time pasa a To finish, we need time, y el significado queda intacto.
teaching.explanationEs: Si puedes quitar palabras sin perder significado, la frase estaba inflada.
segments: A wordy sentence buries its point, so tighten up the draft: In order to finish,
we need time becomes To finish, we need time, and the meaning is untouched.
teaching.audioText: A wordy sentence buries its point, so tighten up the draft: In order to finish, we need time becomes To finish, we need time, and the meaning is untouched.

teaching.en: Needless repetition makes a sentence wordy: the recently opened shop carries the whole idea, whereas the new, recently opened shop says it twice.
teaching.es: La repetición innecesaria vuelve prolija una frase: the recently opened shop contiene toda la idea, mientras que the new, recently opened shop la dice dos veces.
teaching.explanationEs: New y recently opened cuentan la misma idea: basta con uno de los dos.
segments: Needless repetition makes a sentence wordy: the recently opened shop carries the
whole idea, whereas the new, recently opened shop says it twice.
teaching.audioText: Needless repetition makes a sentence wordy: the recently opened shop carries the whole idea, whereas the new, recently opened shop says it twice.

teaching.en: A lapse in tense is easy to miss, so keep the timeline steady: when the manager arrived, the team had already finished the report and sent it to the council.
teaching.es: Un desliz en el tiempo verbal es fácil de pasar por alto, así que mantén estable la cronología: cuando llegó el jefe, el equipo ya había terminado el informe y se lo había enviado al consejo.
teaching.explanationEs: Lo anterior a otro hecho pasado lleva had + participio; no mezcles tiempos sin motivo.
segments: A lapse in tense is easy to miss, so keep the timeline steady: when the
manager arrived, the team had already finished the report and sent it to the council.
teaching.audioText: A lapse in tense is easy to miss, so keep the timeline steady: when the manager arrived, the team had already finished the report and sent it to the council.

teaching.en: Colloquial phrasing and vague quantities weaken a report, and ambiguity is best removed with exact wording: forty interviews, not a lot of interviews.
teaching.es: La redacción coloquial y las cantidades vagas debilitan un informe, y la ambigüedad se elimina mejor con palabras exactas: cuarenta entrevistas, no muchas entrevistas.
teaching.explanationEs: El registro profesional prefiere cifras y expresiones precisas a fórmulas de conversación.
segments: Colloquial phrasing and vague quantities weaken a report, and ambiguity is best
removed with exact wording: forty interviews, not a lot of interviews.
teaching.audioText: Colloquial phrasing and vague quantities weaken a report, and ambiguity is best removed with exact wording: forty interviews, not a lot of interviews.

prompt.es: Marca 1: elige el conector que respeta la lógica del párrafo.

choices.text: nevertheless
consequently
meanwhile

feedback.es: Revisar el presupuesto es la consecuencia de la mayor asistencia; nevertheless marca contraste y meanwhile sitúa los hechos en paralelo.

hint.es: El segundo hecho es la consecuencia del primero.

origin.text: The library extended its opening hours in March. Attendance rose by a fifth; ___, the budget for cleaning had to be revised.

prompt.es: Completa: «A pesar del retraso, el informe llegó al consejo a tiempo.»

feedback.es: Despite introduce un contraste formal y se une directamente al nombre: despite the delay, sin of.

hint.es: Preposición de contraste que va seguida del nombre sin of.

origin.text: We postponed the survey twice. ___ the delay, the final report still reached the council before the deadline.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Tras revisar el borrador, eliminó toda repetición innecesaria.»

answer.text: Having reviewed the draft, she removed every needless repetition

feedback.es: Having + participio presenta la acción previa y deja un solo sujeto para toda la frase.

hint.es: Empieza con la acción anterior, expresada con having.

prompt.es: Marca 4: ¿qué versión conserva el sentido con menos palabras?

choices.text: On account of the fact that the committee had failed to decide, the vote was put off until next week.
The vote was postponed until next week because the committee was in a position of not having decided.
As the committee had failed to decide, the vote was postponed until next week.
The vote was postponed.

feedback.es: As the committee had failed to decide conserva causa y plazo con menos palabras; la opción más breve pierde información.

origin.text: The minutes of the meeting state: Due to the fact that the committee failed to reach a decision on the matter, the vote was postponed until the following week.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige el principio que ilustra el cambio de la editora.

choices.text: An exact number is far more convincing than a loose impression.
A shorter phrase is always better than a longer one.
A formal connector should replace an informal one.

feedback.es: La editora sustituye una cantidad vaga por una cifra: la precisión hace la frase más creíble, no solo más corta.

origin.audio: In the draft, the writer said that a lot of participants had dropped out. The editor circled the phrase and asked how many. Six of the forty, it turned out. She replaced the phrase with six of the forty participants, and the sentence suddenly carried weight instead of suggestion.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con la relación lógica que establece el conector.

pairs: The roads were closed; consequently, deliveries slipped.
The roads were closed; nevertheless, deliveries arrived.
The roads were closed; moreover, the main bridge was damaged.
Several roads were closed; for instance, the ring road.
The roads were closed, since the river had risen.

feedback.es: Elegir bien el conector depende de la relación real entre las ideas: consecuencia, contraste, suma, ejemplo o causa.

pairs: The roads were closed; consequently, deliveries slipped.
The roads were closed; nevertheless, deliveries arrived.
The roads were closed; moreover, the main bridge was damaged.
Several roads were closed; for instance, the ring road.
The roads were closed, since the river had risen.

prompt.es: Marca 7: corrige el registro y el conector de esta frase del borrador.

answer.text: The figures were rather poor; nevertheless, the board decided to continue with the trial.
accepted: The figures were rather poor; nevertheless, the board decided to continue with the trial.
The figures were somewhat weak; even so, the board decided to go ahead with the trial.
The figures were fairly poor; however, the board decided to carry on with the trial.

feedback.es: El cambio mínimo sustituye pretty bad por una expresión neutra y so por un conector de contraste, porque decidir seguir contradice la decepción.

origin.text: The figures were pretty bad, so the board decided to go ahead with the trial anyway.

evidenceGroups: in spite of this the board

prompt.es: Completa: «Hay que ajustar este párrafo: la mitad de las palabras no aportan nada.»

feedback.es: Tighten up es la colocación habitual para hacer más concisa una sección sin cambiar su contenido.

origin.text: The second paragraph repeats the first in different words. We need to ___ up the whole section, because half of the words add nothing.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué sugiere Mia al proponer que Tom lo lea en voz alta.

choices.text: That Tom should rewrite the argument, which she does not find persuasive.
That speaking the text reveals slips the eye skips over.
That the report will persuade the team better if read out loud.

feedback.es: Leer en voz alta es una forma de proofread: el oído detecta cambios de tiempo y repeticiones que la vista pasa por alto.

origin.audio: After reading Tom's draft, Mia did not begin with the errors. She said that the argument was sound and the findings were clear, which made the small problems all the more annoying. Within a single paragraph, the report shifted from past to present, and two paragraphs began with exactly the same sentence. She suggested that he proofread it aloud and then delete every sentence that said the same thing twice. Tom wondered whether she was only being kind, but she insisted that the content was good and the packaging only messy.

prompt.es: Marca 12: ¿a qué se refiere «Such a pattern» en la última frase?

choices.text: To the little time students spend between their classes.
To the difficulty of changing such a habit once formed.
To phone-checking taking the place of conversation.

feedback.es: Such a pattern retoma lo descrito en las dos frases anteriores: mirar el móvil en lugar de conversar.

origin.text: Many students check their phones between classes. This, in turn, shortens the time they spend talking to one another. Such a pattern is hard to change once it sets in.

prompt.es: ¿Qué pretende en realidad la autora de este mensaje sobre el borrador?

choices.text: To praise the draft and leave it exactly as it is.
To suggest that the second section be expanded.
To ask tactfully for a cut she considers necessary.
To cancel the discussion planned for Thursday.

feedback.es: Tras los elogios, «I wonder whether… might be shortened» es una petición cortés pero real de recorte; el resto suaviza el mensaje.

origin.text: Thank you for the draft. The structure is promising, and the examples are well chosen. I wonder, though, whether the second section might be shortened; as it stands, the point arrives rather slowly, and the reader may lose the thread before the first example appears. Perhaps we could discuss it on Thursday, if that suits you.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Cuando llegó el director, ya habíamos terminado el informe.»

answer.text: By the time the director arrived, we had already finished the report
accepted: By the time the director arrived, we had already finished the report
We had already finished the report by the time the director arrived

feedback.es: By the time + pasado simple fija el momento, y lo anterior a él va en pasado perfecto: had already finished.

prompt.es: Marca 11: sustituye el registro coloquial por uno profesional.

answer.text: We made an error in the figures, and the manager was unhappy about it.
accepted: We made an error in the figures, and the manager was unhappy about it.
We made a mistake in the figures, and the director was annoyed about it.
We miscalculated the figures, and the supervisor was dissatisfied about it.

feedback.es: En un informe se evita la expresión de conversación: un sustantivo neutro para el fallo y un adjetivo formal para la reacción mantienen el sentido.

origin.text: We kind of messed up the figures, and the boss was pretty mad about it.
